title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for cancer treatment.

HPI
Pt is a 71 y.o. male with a known primary colon cancer. Pt is currently receiving chemotherapy for the malignancy. Today’s visit is to address concerns regarding liver metastases identified on recent imaging. Pt reports mild fatigue and some abdominal discomfort but denies acute fevers or severe pain.

Medication List
- Chemotherapy agent (current cycle)
- Ondansetron 8mg PRN for N/V
- Multivitamin daily

Exam
Pt alert and oriented x3. Appears stated age. NAD. Abdomen soft, non-tender, non-distended. Lungs clear to auscultation, RRR. CTAB.

Assessment
1. Colon cancer: Pt is on active treatment for primary malignancy.
2. Liver metastases: Present and being managed as part of systemic therapy.

Plan
- Continue current chemotherapy regimen as scheduled.
- Monitor for toxicity.
- F/u in 4 weeks for reassessment of liver metastasis status and overall tolerance to treatment.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, NP
10/15/2026
explanations: Cancer of the colon under current treatment is a current malignancy: C18.9.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
